label: Angular
existing_comment: Used by BAJ Displaced Joint

label: Arch Shaped Connecting Pipeline
comment: A pipe cross-section with a circular soffit and a flat invert, joined by parallel sides. Used for DCG char1 (E).

label: Atmosphere Within
comment: A potentially hazardous atmosphere (oxygen deficiency, hydrogen sulfide, methane) was detected in the pipe or chamber. Used for BDF (pipe) and DDF (manhole/chamber), with char giving the hazard type as its subclasses.

label: Attached Deposits
comment: Material such as encrustation, grease or fouling is attached to the wall of the pipe or chamber. Used for BBB (pipe) and DBB (manhole/chamber), with char giving the material type as its subclasses.

label: Authority Instruction
din_clause: Table 7, BDC char2 (B); Table 13, DDC char2 (B)
comment: Records that the inspection was terminated on the instruction of the employing authority rather than for a technical reason. Used for BDC char2 (B) and DDC char2 (B).

label: Backdrop Connection
comment: The connecting pipe discharges via a backdrop: an enclosed vertical pipe carrying flow from a higher-level drain down to the manhole invert. Used for DCA char1 (C).

label: Benching
existing_comment:
Describe the benching arrangment of a connection type.

Created for code DCA (Connection Type, Node Inventory Code), char2.

label: Benching Connection
comment: The connecting pipe discharges directly into the benching. Used for DCA char1 (A).

label: Benching Connection Infiltration
existing_comment: Infiltration through the space between a connecting pipe and the wall of the manhole/chamber, above benching

label: Blistered Or Internal Bulge Lining
din_clause: Table 4, BAK char1 (E); Table 10, DAK char1 (E)
comment: The lining has blistered or bulged inward from the host wall. Used for BAK char1 (E) and DAK char1 (E), distinct from Blistering, which is a bulge in the host wall's own surface rather than the lining.

label: Blistering
din_clause: Table 4, BAF char1 (K); Table 10, DAF char1 (K)
comment: An internal bulge in the pipe or chamber wall's own surface, distinct from a lining bulge (BlisteredOrInternalBulgeLining). Used for BAF char1 (K) and DAF char1 (K).

label: Break
existing_comment: pieces of pipe visibly displaced but not missing

label: Break Or Collapse
comment: A structural failure ranging from displaced but still-present pieces, through missing pieces, to a complete loss of structural integrity. Used for BAC (pipe) and DAC (manhole/chamber), with Break, MissingWallBreakOrCollapse and CollapsedBreakOrCollapse as its char subclasses.

label: Broken Plastic Encapsulation Of Step
comment: The plastic coating (encapsulation) around a step has cracked or broken, exposing the metal step beneath to corrosion. Used only for DAQ char (E).

label: Camera Underwater
din_clause: Table 7, BDG char (A); Table 13, DDG char (A)
comment: The view is obstructed because the camera itself is under water. Used for BDG char (A) and DDG char (A).

label: Cause
existing_comment:
`Cause` is used to describe the characterization codes that define the cause of a defect.

Example: Surface Damage `BAF` char2 describes mechanical, chemical, [...] causes for the surface damage.

---


Created to describe BAF / DAF Surface Damage Char2.

Describes the cause of the surface damage. Has potential to be expanded to further describes other damage codes as well.

Also used to described BDG Loss of vision and its reasons for the vision obstruction to the view of the pipeline.

Also to describe DDC InspectionTermination Reasons

label: Channel
existing_comment:
Used to describe DCI char1 and 2:

!Characterisation 1"  The following information:  channel defective (A); channel not defective (B);  !no channel (C)."

!Characterisation 2 Further information:  Channel narrows (in the direction of flow) (A); Channel widens (in the direction of flow) (B); Channel has a high point (C); Channel has a low point (D)."

label: Channel In Benching
comment: The connecting pipe's channel runs within the benching itself, one of four benching-arrangement diagrams in the standard. Used for DCA char2 (A).

label: Chemical
din_clause: Table 4, BAF char2 (B); Table 10, DAF char2 (B)
comment: One of the listed causes of surface damage, denoting general chemical attack on the wall. Used for BAF char2 (B) and DAF char2 (B), and is the parent of ChemicalUpperPart and ChemicalLowerPart, which record where in the cross-section the chemical damage occurs.

label: Chemical Lower Part
din_clause: Table 4, BAF char2 (D); Table 10, DAF char2 (D)
comment: Chemical surface damage located in the lower part of the pipe or channel. Used for BAF char2 (D) and DAF char2 (D), distinguished from ChemicalUpperPart by location in the cross-section.

label: Chemical Upper Part
din_clause: Table 4, BAF char2 (C); Table 10, DAF char2 (C)
comment: Chemical surface damage located in the upper part of the pipe or channel. Used for BAF char2 (C) and DAF char2 (C), distinguished from ChemicalLowerPart by location in the cross-section.

label: Chiselled Plain Connection
comment: A connection made without any special fitting, through a rough hole formed with a hammer and chisel. Used for BCA char1 (E), distinguished from DrilledPlainConnection by the hole-forming method.

label: Chiselled Saddle Connection
comment: A connection made using a saddle fitting through a rough hole formed with a hammer and chisel. Used for BCA char1 (C), distinguished from DrilledSaddleConnection by the hole-forming method.

label: Clear Effluent Wastewater
din_clause: Table 7, BDD (A); BDE char1 (A); DDE char1 (A)
comment: The wastewater is clear enough that the invert is visible. Used for BDD (A), BDE char1 (A) and DDE char1 (A).

label: Closed Connection
comment: Records that the connection has been closed off; either a junction left for future use or one that has been cut off. Used for BCA char2 (B).

label: Coarse Settled Deposit
din_clause: Table 5, BBC char (B); Table 11, DBC char (B)
comment: Coarse settled material such as rubble or gravel. Used for BBC char (B) and DBC char (B).

label: Collapsed Break Or Collapse
existing_comment: complete loss of structural integrity

label: Coloured Wastewater
comment: The wastewater is coloured; the combined 'turbid and coloured' value (E) is also mapped onto this class. Used for BDD (D)/(E) and BDE char1 (D)/(E).

label: Connecting Pipeline
comment: Details of a pipeline connecting to the manhole or inspection chamber, primarily its cross-sectional shape. Used for DCG char1, with the specific shapes as subclasses; the pipe-side standard has no equivalent code, since a connecting pipeline's shape there is only captured in BCA's remarks.

label: Connecting Pipeline Discharge Direction
existing_comment:
To define DCG char2:

Whether the connection is incoming or outgoing or has been sealed:  connection discharges into the manhole or inspection chamber (A); connection discharges from the manhole or inspection chamber (B); connection closed (C).

label: Connection
comment: Another pipeline is connected to the pipe being inspected; most such connections are assumed circular unless recorded otherwise. Used for BCA (pipe); the node-side connection concept is instead split across NodeConnection (DCA) and ConnectingPipeline (DCG).

label: Connection Discharge Bneching
comment: The connection discharges across the surface of the benching rather than through a formed channel. Used for DCA char2 (B).

label: Connection Not Evident
comment: Records that the type of connection fitting could not be determined during inspection. Used for BCA char1 (G).

label: Continuation Flow Control
comment: Records that the flow-control device controls the continuing (foul-water) flow rather than an overflow. Used for DCK char2 (A).

label: Correct Connection
din_clause: Table 7, BDE char2 (C); Table 13, DDE char2 (C)
comment: The connecting pipe was not observed to be wrongly connected. Used for BDE char2 (C) and DDE char2 (C).

label: Crack Fissure
din_clause: Table 4, BAB char1 (B); Table 10, DAB char1 (B)
comment: A fissure where crack lines are visible on the wall but the pieces remain in place; more severe than a surface crack but not yet an open fracture. Used for BAB char1 (B) and DAB char1 (B).

label: Crack Or Split Or Weld Failure
din_clause: Table 4, BAK char1 (I); Table 10, DAK char1 (I)
comment: The lining has a crack, a split, or a failed weld. Used for BAK char1 (I) and DAK char1 (I); DIN treats these three distinct fault types as a single characterization value, which SDCO mirrors in one class rather than splitting them.

label: Cross Section
existing_comment:
Used to describe DCO.

DCO Characterisation The shape of the horizontal (plan) cross-section of the manhole or inspection  chamber as follows:  circular (A); rectangular (B);  local section - code to be specified by the employing authority and prefixed by an X (e.g. XA);  !other (Z) – where this is used

label: Defect
comment: The standard groups its fabric-condition and operation-condition main codes (BA../BB.. for pipes, DA../DB.. for nodes) under these two editorial headings, without restricting how the codes may be combined. SDCO mirrors that split with StructuralDefect and OperationalDefect as the two children of Defect.

label: Defective Benching
comment: Records that the benching is defective. Used for DCH char (A).

label: Defective Brickwork Or Masonry
comment: Individual bricks or masonry units of a brick/masonry pipe or chamber have moved, gone missing, or (pipes only) let the invert drop, from their original position. Used for BAD (pipe) and DAD (manhole/chamber).

label: Defective Channel
comment: Records that the channel is defective. Used for DCI char1 (A).

label: Defective Connection
comment: A connection to the pipe or chamber is faulty; wrongly positioned, gapped, damaged or blocked. Used for BAH (pipe) and DAH (manhole/chamber), with char giving the specific defect type as its subclasses.

label: Defective Cover Or Frame
comment: There is a defect in the manhole or inspection chamber cover or frame; broken, rocking, missing, or set above/below the surrounding surface level. Used only for DAR; the standard defines no pipe-side equivalent, since pipes have no cover.

label: Defective Repair
comment: A previously carried-out repair to the pipe or chamber wall now itself has a defect. Used for BAL (pipe, requires the BCB point-repair code too) and DAL (manhole/chamber, requires DCB too), with char1 giving the specific defect type.

label: Defective Step Or Ladder
comment: There is a defect in an access step, ladder or toe hole inside a manhole or inspection chamber. Used only for DAQ; the standard defines no pipe-side equivalent, since pipes have no steps or ladders.

label: Deformation
comment: The cross-sectional shape of the pipe or chamber has changed from its original shape, either generally across a wide area or as a localised deformation. Used for BAA (pipe) and DAA (manhole/chamber); DAA further splits into GeneralDeformation and LocalisedDeformation, a distinction BAA does not make.

label: Discountinued Wastewater Code
din_clause: Table 7, BDD (B); BDE char1 (B); DDE char1 (B)
comment: A wastewater-appearance value retained from an earlier edition of the standard whose use has since been discontinued. Used for BDD (B), BDE char1 (B) and DDE char1 (B).

label: Displaced Joint
comment: Adjacent pipe units, or adjacent chamber units, are displaced out of their intended alignment relative to each other. Used for BAJ (pipe, char: longitudinal/radial/angular) and DAJ (manhole/chamber, char: vertical/horizontal/angular); the two codes reuse different sets of Orientation values for the same displacement concept.

label: Displaced Sealing Ring
din_clause: Table 4, BAI char2 (A); Table 10, DAI char2 (A)
comment: The sealing ring is visibly displaced from its joint but is not intruding into the bore. Used for BAI char2 (A) and DAI char2 (A).

label: Drilled Plain Connection
comment: A connection made without any special fitting, through a neat, drilled hole. Used for BCA char1 (D), distinguished from ChiselledPlainConnection by the hole-forming method.

label: Drilled Saddle Connection
comment: A connection made using a saddle fitting through a neat, drilled hole. Used for BCA char1 (B), distinguished from ChiselledSaddleConnection by the hole-forming method.

label: Dripping Infiltration
din_clause: Table 5, BBF char (B); Table 11, DBF char1 (B)
comment: Water enters as intermittent drips rather than a continuous flow. Used for BBF char (B) and DBF char1 (B).

label: Dropped Invert Brickwork Or Masonry
comment: A section of the invert of a brick or masonry pipeline has dropped relative to the walls, leaving a gap of more than 20 mm. Used only for BAD char1 (C); DIN defines no equivalent DAD value for manholes/chambers.

label: Egg Shaped Connecting Pipeline
comment: A pipe cross-section shaped like an egg (narrower top, wider bottom). Used for DCG char1 (C).

label: Equipment Failure
din_clause: Table 7, BDC char1 (C); Table 13, DDC char1 (D)
comment: One of the listed reasons an inspection was terminated early, denoting a failure of the inspection equipment itself. Used for BDC char1 (C) and DDC char1 (D).

label: Exfiltration
comment: Visible leakage of flow out of the pipe or chamber. Used for BBG (pipe) and DBG (manhole/chamber); neither code carries any characterization or quantification.

label: External Pipes Or Cables Built Through Structure Obstacle
Fine Settled Deposit
din_clause: Table 5, BBC char (A); Table 11, DBC char (A)
comment: Fine settled material such as sand or silt. Used for BBC char (A) and DBC char (A).

label: Fissure
comment: A crack in the pipe or chamber wall, ranging from a surface-only crack through visible crack lines to a fully open fracture. Used for BAB (pipe) and DAB (manhole/chamber), with SurfaceCrackFissure, CrackFissure and FractureFissure as its char1 subclasses.

label: Float Operated Gate Valve Flow Control
Flow Control
existing_comment: Used to describe DCK: Flow Control

label: Flow From Incoming Pipe
comment: Information about the wastewater flowing from an incoming/connecting pipe, requiring the connection code (BCA, or DCA+DCG) to also be recorded. Used for BDE (pipe) and DDE (manhole/chamber), with char1 giving the water's appearance (shared with Wastewater) and char2 flagging a wrongly-connected pipe.

label: Flowing Infiltration
din_clause: Table 5, BBF char (C); Table 11, DBF char1 (C)
comment: Water enters as a continuous flow. Used for BBF char (C) and DBF char1 (C).

label: Fouling Attached Deposit
din_clause: Table 5, BBB char (C); Table 11, DBB char (C)
comment: A deposit of organisms (e.g. biofilm) attached to the wall, as opposed to encrustation or grease. Used for BBB char (C) and DBB char (C).

label: Fracture Fissure
din_clause: Table 4, BAB char1 (C); Table 10, DAB char1 (C)
comment: The most severe fissure type: a crack visibly open in the wall, though the pieces are still in place. Used for BAB char1 (C) and DAB char1 (C).

label: Free Drop Connection
comment: The connecting pipe discharges as a free fall (an open drop) into the channel. Used for DCA char1 (B).

label: Gap Connection
din_clause: Table 4, BAH char (B); Table 10, DAH char (B)
comment: There is a gap all the way around the connecting pipe's junction with the main pipe or chamber wall. Used for BAH char (B) and DAH char (B), distinguished from PartialGapConnection by extending around the full circumference.

label: General Photograph
comment: A still photograph taken to record the general condition of the pipe or chamber rather than a specific coded feature. Used for BDA (pipe) and DDA (manhole/chamber).

label: General Remark
comment: A free-text remark that cannot be captured by any other code. Used for BDB (pipe) and DDB (manhole/chamber).

label: Grit Trap Under Cover
existing_comment:
Used to describe DCM.

DCM This is used to record the presence of a grit trap (bucket) under the cover.  Characterisation The following information:  trap present with no defects (A); trap missing (with evidence that one was provided) (B); trap defective (C).

label: Gushing Infiltration
din_clause: Table 5, BBF char (D); Table 11, DBF char1 (D)
comment: The most severe infiltration extent: water entering under pressure. Used for BBF char (D) and DBF char1 (D).

label: Hard Or Compacted Settled Deposit
din_clause: Table 5, BBC char (C); Table 11, DBC char (C)
comment: Hard or compacted settled material such as concrete. Used for BBC char (C) and DBC char (C).

label: High Point Channel
comment: The channel has a high point (a local rise against the flow direction). Used for DCI char2 (C).

label: High Water Level
din_clause: Table 7, BDC char1 (B); Table 13, DDC char1 (C)
comment: One of the listed reasons an inspection was terminated early, denoting a water level too high to continue. Used for BDC char1 (B) and DDC char1 (C).

label: Hole Repair
din_clause: Table 6, BCB char1 (E); Table 12, DCB char (D)
comment: A hole was repaired directly (e.g. patched) rather than by lining, injection or replacement. Used for DCB char (D); the corresponding pipe-side value (BCB char1 E) has no someValuesFrom wiring, so only node individuals currently materialize into this class.

label: Hydrogen Sulfide
din_clause: Table 7, BDF char (B); Table 13, DDF char (B)
comment: Hydrogen sulfide gas was detected in the atmosphere. Used for BDF char (B) and DDF char (B).

label: In Manhole Or Inspection Chamber
comment: The vermin was seen in the manhole or inspection chamber itself, the node-side counterpart of the pipe-side InPipeline value. Used for DBH char2 (A).

label: In Pipeline
comment: The vermin was seen in the pipeline itself, one of the listed vermin-location values used for pipe inspections. Used for BBH char2 (A); the node-side equivalent value is instead InManholeOrInspectionChamber (DBH char2 A), since the location described differs for the two structures.

label: Infiltration
comment: Water ingressing into the pipe or chamber through the wall, joints or defects. Used for BBF (pipe, char: sweating/dripping/flowing/gushing extent) and DBF (manhole/chamber, char1 extent + char2 entry point: wall, invert connection, or benching connection); DBF adds an entry-location characterization that BBF does not have.

label: Ingress Of Soil
comment: Soil from the surrounding ground is intruding into the pipe or chamber. Used for BBD (pipe, with char giving the soil type as subclasses) and DBD (manhole/chamber); DIN gives DBD no characterization codes, so the soil-type subclasses only ever classify pipe individuals.

label: Injected Mortar Repair
comment: Mortar was injected to repair the defect, a pipe-only repair method. Corresponds to BCB char1 (C); has no someValuesFrom wiring to hasPipeInventoryFeature, so this class is not currently reachable through materialization; DIN's node-side equivalent (DCB C, injection of sealing material) is instead mapped to InjectedSealingMaterialRepair.

label: Injected Sealing Material Repair
din_clause: Table 6, BCB char1 (D); Table 12, DCB char (C)
comment: A sealing material other than mortar was injected to repair the defect. Used for DCB char (C); on the pipe side this corresponds to BCB char1 (D), which has no someValuesFrom wiring, so only node individuals currently materialize into this class.

label: Inspection Complete
din_clause: Table 7, BDC char2 (A)/(C); Table 13, DDC char2 (A)
comment: Records that, taken with a previous partial inspection, the whole pipeline is now complete. Used for BDC char2 (C); SDCO also maps the distinct 'objective achieved' values (BDC char2 A, DDC char2 A) onto this same class, conflating two different DIN characterization meanings under one class name.

label: Inspection Incomplete
comment: Records that, taken with a previous partial inspection, the whole pipeline is still not complete. Used only for BDC char2 (D); DIN defines no DDC char2 equivalent since manholes/chambers are not inspected in successive partial passes.

label: Inspection Status
comment: Groups the standard's second termination-reason characterization, which records how a terminated pipe inspection relates to a previously completed partial inspection of the same pipeline. SDCO collects InspectionComplete, InspectionIncomplete, InspectionStatusUnknown and PreviousPartialInspection under this parent.

label: Inspection Status Unknown
comment: Records that it is not known whether, taken with a previous partial inspection, the whole pipeline is now complete. Used only for BDC char2 (E); DIN defines no DDC char2 equivalent.

label: Inspection Termination
comment: The inspection was terminated before reaching the intended finish node (pipe) or before completion (node); any obstruction causing this shall also be coded separately with its own main code. Used for BDC (pipe) and DDC (manhole/chamber), with the Cause subtree giving the termination reason and outcome as subclasses.

label: Internal Drop Pipe Connection
comment: The connecting pipe discharges via an internal drop pipe fitted inside the chamber, distinct from an external backdrop pipe. Used for DCA char1 (D).

label: Internal Film Or Coating Separation
din_clause: Table 4, BAK char1 (G); Table 10, DAK char1 (G)
comment: The internal film or coating layer of a lining has separated from the host wall. Used for BAK char1 (G) and DAK char1 (G).

label: Intruding Broken Sealing Ring
din_clause: Table 4, BAI char2 (D); Table 10, DAI char2 (C)
comment: The sealing ring is both intruding into the bore and broken. Used for BAI char2 (D) and DAI char2 (C).

label: Intruding But Not Broken Sealing Ring
comment: The node-side sealing ring is intruding but not broken; unlike the pipe-side code, DIN does not split this by centreline position for manholes/chambers. Used only for DAI char2 (B).

label: Intruding Connection
comment: A connecting pipe projects into the main pipe or chamber, obstructing its cross-section. Used for BAG (pipe, requires the BCA connection code too) and DAG (node, requires DCA and DCG too).

label: Intruding Sealing Material
comment: Material used to seal a joint between adjacent pipe or chamber units is intruding into the bore. Used for BAI (pipe) and DAI (manhole/chamber), with char1 distinguishing a sealing ring from other sealant.

label: Intruding Sealing Ring
din_clause: Table 4, BAI char1 (A); Table 10, DAI char1 (A)
comment: The intruding sealing material is a sealing ring rather than another kind of sealant. Used for BAI char1 (A) and DAI char1 (A); its own char2 subclasses record whether the ring is displaced, intruding, or broken.

label: Intruding Sealing Ring Above Centreline
comment: The sealing ring is intruding but not broken, with its lowest point above the horizontal centreline. Used only for BAI char2 (B); DIN's node-side char2 has no centreline split; it only distinguishes intruding-but-not-broken (IntrudingButNotBrokenSealingRing) from broken.

label: Intruding Sealing Ring Below Centreline
comment: The sealing ring is intruding but not broken, with its lowest point below the horizontal centreline. Used only for BAI char2 (C); see IntrudingSealingRingAboveCentreline for the corresponding node-side simplification.

label: Inventory
comment: The standard's inventory codes (BC.. for pipes, DC.. for nodes) record permanent fixtures and construction features of the network rather than defects. SDCO groups the corresponding classes (Connection, PointRepair, SewerCurvature, NodeType, Benching, Channel, FlowControl, etc.) under Inventory.

label: Invert Connection Infiltration
existing_comment: Infiltration through the space between a connecting pipe and the wall of the manhole/chamber, at the invert

label: Junction
comment: The connection is made using a prefabricated pipe unit with a factory-formed junction, rather than a fitting added on site. Used for BCA char1 (A).

label: Lamp Hole
comment: A small-diameter vertical access shaft to a drain, too narrow for personnel entry, used mainly for rodding rather than inspection access. Used for BCD (D) and BCE (D).

label: Layer Brickwork Or Masonry Visible
din_clause: Table 4, BAD char2 (A); Table 10, DAD char2 (A)
comment: Where brickwork or masonry is missing, another layer of brickwork or masonry is visible through the hole. Used for BAD char2 (A) and DAD char2 (A).

label: Lining
comment: A defect observed in a pipe or chamber lining (detachment, discolouration, wrinkling, blistering, cracking, holes and similar). Used for BAK (pipe) and DAK (manhole/chamber), with char1 giving the specific lining fault as its subclasses.

label: Lining Connection Defect
din_clause: Table 4, BAK char1 (K); Table 10, DAK char1 (K)
comment: There is a defect where the lining meets a connection rather than in the lining's main run. Used for BAK char1 (K) and DAK char1 (K).

label: Localised Lining Of Connection Repair
din_clause: Table 6, BCB char1 (F); Table 12, DCB char (E)
comment: A short localised lining (e.g. a 'top hat') was applied to repair a connection rather than the main wall. Used for DCB char (E); the pipe-side equivalent (BCB char1 F) has no someValuesFrom wiring, so only node individuals currently materialize into this class.

label: Localised Lining Of Manhole Or Inspection Chamber Repair
comment: A short section of lining was applied inside the manhole or inspection chamber as the repair method. Used for DCB char (B); its pipe-side equivalent is LocalisedLiningOfPipeRepair (BCB char1 B), which has no someValuesFrom wiring.

label: Localised Lining Of Pipe Repair
comment: A short section of pipe lining was applied as the repair method; DIN notes this combination should also be coded with BAK (Lining). Corresponds to BCB char1 (B); has no someValuesFrom wiring to hasPipeInventoryFeature, so it is not currently reachable through materialization.

label: Location
Loss Of Vision
existing_comment: Reasons for loss of vision captured in subclass 'Cause'

label: Low Point Channel
comment: The channel has a low point (a local dip below the surrounding invert). Used for DCI char2 (D).

label: Major Connection Without Manhole Or Inspection Chamber
comment: The node is simply a significant connection point (e.g. a large junction) without any manhole or inspection chamber structure built around it. Used for BCD (F) and BCE (F).

label: Mechanical
din_clause: Table 4, BAF char2 (A); Table 10, DAF char2 (A)
comment: One of the listed causes of surface damage, denoting physical/mechanical action rather than chemical attack. Used for BAF char2 (A) and DAF char2 (A), the cause dimension of the Surface Damage code.

label: Methane
din_clause: Table 7, BDF char (C); Table 13, DDF char (C)
comment: Methane gas was detected in the atmosphere. Used for BDF char (C) and DDF char (C).

label: Missing Brickwork Or Masonry
din_clause: Table 4, BAD char1 (B); Table 10, DAD char1 (B), DAE
comment: Bricks or masonry units are missing from the pipe or chamber wall. Used for BAD char1 (B) and DAD char1 (B); SDCO also maps the separate node-only DAE (Missing mortar) code onto this class rather than a distinct node-side MissingMortar class, so this class conflates two different DIN observations for manhole individuals.

label: Missing Mortar
comment: All or part of the mortar bedding a brick or masonry pipe wall is missing. Used only for BAE (pipe); SDCO maps DAE, the mirroring node-side missing-mortar code, onto MissingBrickworkOrMasonry instead of this class, so MissingMortar never classifies node individuals.

label: Missing Wall Break Or Collapse
existing_comment: missing pieces of wall

label: Narrows Channel
comment: The channel narrows in the direction of flow. Used for DCI char2 (A).

label: No Benching
comment: Records that the manhole or inspection chamber has no benching. Used for DCH char (C).

label: No Channel
comment: Records that the manhole or inspection chamber has no channel. Used for DCI char1 (C).

label: Node Connection
comment: The node-side connection-type characterization: how a pipeline enters the manhole or inspection chamber (in the benching, free drop, backdrop, internal drop pipe, ramp, ventilation). Used for DCA char1, with the specific arrangement types as subclasses.

label: Node Type
comment: The type of node; manhole, inspection chamber, rodding eye, lamp hole, outfall, major connection without a chamber, or an employing-authority-defined type; at the start or finish of the pipeline inspection. Used for BCD (start node) and BCE (finish node), which share the same characterization values as this class's subclasses.

label: Not Evident
din_clause: Table 4, BAF char2 (E); Table 10, DAF char2 (E)
comment: Records that surface damage was observed but its cause could not be determined. Used for BAF char2 (E) and DAF char2 (E).

label: Nothing Visible
din_clause: Table 4, BAD char2 (B); Table 10, DAD char2 (B)
comment: Where brickwork or masonry is missing, it is not possible to determine what is exposed through the hole. Used for BAD char2 (B) and DAD char2 (B).

label: Observation
comment: DIN EN 13508-2 requires every recorded feature to be tagged with one of its defined main codes, optionally refined by characterization, quantification and location information. SDCO's Observation class is the root of the damage-code taxonomy, spanning both pipe (B-codes) and node (D-codes) observations across its six subtrees (Cause, Defect, Inventory, Location, Orientation, OtherObservation).

label: Obstacle
comment: An object in the manhole or inspection chamber obstructing its cross-section, used only when none of the other operational codes (roots, deposits, soil) apply. Used for DBE; SDCO maps the pipe-side equivalent (BBE) onto OtherObstacle instead of this class, so Obstacle itself only ever classifies node individuals.

label: Obstruction
din_clause: Table 7, BDC char1 (A); Table 13, DDC char1 (B)
comment: One of the listed reasons an inspection was terminated early, denoting a physical obstruction blocking the camera or equipment. Used for BDC char1 (A) and DDC char1 (B).

label: Open Connection
comment: Records that the connection is open and in use. Used for BCA char2 (A).

label: Operational Defect
comment: Groups the standard's operation-condition codes (BB.. for pipes, DB.. for nodes); roots, deposits, obstacles, infiltration, exfiltration, vermin; describing how debris, water or organisms affect the running of the pipe or chamber rather than its fabric. SDCO uses OperationalDefect as the parent of these classes, referenced via hasPipeOperationDamage/hasNodeOperationDamage.

label: Orientation
comment: The standard records the clockface position of an observation and, for several defects, an orientation value (longitudinal/circumferential/vertical/horizontal/complex/helical/inclined/radial/angular) describing how the feature runs relative to the pipe or chamber axis. SDCO collects all such orientation-valued classes under this parent, referenced from hasDamageOrientation and the curvature-direction properties.

label: Orifice Plate Flow Control
comment: A plate with a fixed opening used to restrict or regulate flow. Used for DCK char1 (C).

label: Other Cause
existing_comment: General catch all for any other cause / obstructions described in several damage codes.

label: Other Connection Repair
din_clause: Table 6, BCB char1 (G); Table 12, DCB char (F)
comment: Some other repair method (not localised lining) was applied to a connection. Used for DCB char (F); the pipe-side equivalent (BCB char1 G) has no someValuesFrom wiring, so only node individuals currently materialize into this class.

label: Other Observation
existing_comment: Describes the codes categorized as 'Other' in DIN EN 13508-2.

label: Other Obstacle
comment: Covers the pipe-side obstacle code (BBE) generically, plus the catch-all 'other' obstacle type on both sides. Used for BBE, BBE char (Z) and DBE char (Z); this conflates the plain pipe main-code with the DIN 'other' characterization value, unlike the node side, where Obstacle is the main-code parent.

label: Other Pipeline Through Manhole
existing_comment:
To describe DCL.

DCL !There is another wastewater pipeline through the manhole or inspection  chamber.  The connections to the manhole or inspection chamber joined to each end of the pipeline should be coded using DCA and DCG." Characterisation 1 There is:  no access to the pipe (A); access is provided – cover in place (B);  !access is provided – cover missing (C)."  Characterisation 2 !The pipeline is:"  defective (A); not defective (B).

label: Other Point Repair
comment: Some other repair method was used, with further detail in the remarks. Used for DCB char (Z); the pipe-side equivalent (BCB char1 Z, OtherTrenchlessRepair) has no someValuesFrom wiring.

label: Other Trenchless Repair
comment: Some other trenchless repair method was used, with further detail in the remarks. Corresponds to BCB char1 (Z); has no someValuesFrom wiring to hasPipeInventoryFeature, so it is not currently reachable through materialization.

label: Oval Connecting Pipeline
comment: A pipe cross-section with equal-diameter circular invert and soffit, joined by parallel sides. Used for DCG char1 (F).

label: Overflow Control
comment: Records that the flow-control device controls an overflow rather than the continuing flow. Used for DCK char2 (B).

label: Oxygen Deficiency
din_clause: Table 7, BDF char (A); Table 13, DDF char (A)
comment: A shortage of oxygen was detected in the atmosphere. Used for BDF char (A) and DDF char (A).

label: Partial Gap Connection
din_clause: Table 4, BAH char (C); Table 10, DAH char (C)
comment: There is a gap around only part of the circumference of the connecting pipe's junction. Used for BAH char (C) and DAH char (C), distinguished from GapConnection by covering only part of the circumference.

label: Patch Sealing Defective Repair
din_clause: Table 4, BAL char1 (B); Table 10, DAL char (B)
comment: A patch that was used to seal a hole deliberately cut in the wall (e.g. for a connection) has itself become defective. Used for BAL char1 (B) and DAL char (B).

label: Pipe Connection
comment: The pipe-side connection-type characterization: how the connecting pipe was formed into the wall (prefabricated junction, drilled or chiselled saddle/plain fitting, not evident). Used for BCA char1, with the specific fitting types as subclasses.

label: Pipe Replaced Repair
comment: A section of pipe was replaced during the repair. Corresponds to BCB char1 (A); unlike its node counterpart (DCB char A to WallPartRepair), this class currently has no someValuesFrom restriction wiring it to hasPipeInventoryFeature, so BCB (A) individuals are not classified into it by materialization.

label: Pipe Under Benching
comment: The connecting pipe passes underneath the benching rather than discharging across or through it. Used for DCA char2 (D).

label: Point Repair
comment: A short section of the drain, sewer, manhole or inspection chamber has been repaired using a listed method (replacement, lining, injected material, hole repair). Used for BCB (pipe) and DCB (manhole/chamber), with char giving the repair method as its subclasses.

label: Porous Pipe
comment: The pipe material is observed to be porous. Used only for BAN; DIN's mirroring node code (DAN, Porous wall) is modelled in SDCO as the separate PorousWall class rather than merged into this one.

label: Porous Wall
comment: The material forming the manhole or inspection chamber wall is observed to be porous. Used only for DAN, the node-side counterpart of BAN (Porous pipe).

label: Previous Partial Inspection
comment: Marks that the termination reason relates to a previous partial inspection of the same pipeline, and is the parent of the three specific completeness outcomes. Referenced by BDC char2 (C), (D) and (E).

label: Radial
existing_comment: used by BAJ Displaced Joint

label: Ramp Channel Benching
comment: The connection's channel forms a ramp down through the benching to the main channel. Used for DCA char2 (C).

label: Ramp Connection
comment: The connecting pipe discharges via a ramp leading down to the channel. Used for DCA char1 (E).

label: Repair Material Separated
din_clause: Table 4, BAL char1 (C); Table 10, DAL char (C)
comment: The repair material has separated from the host wall it was applied to. Used for BAL char1 (C) and DAL char (C).

label: Resin Missing From Laminate
din_clause: Table 4, BAK char1 (M); Table 10, DAK char1 (M)
comment: Resin is missing from a laminate lining, exposing the underlying fibre reinforcement. Used for BAK char1 (M) and DAK char1 (M).

label: Rodding Eye
comment: A surface-level access point allowing rodding equipment to be inserted into the pipe without an inspection chamber. Used for BCD (C) and BCE (C).

label: Roots
comment: Roots of trees or other plants have grown into the pipe or chamber through joints, defects or connections. Used for BBA (pipe) and DBA (manhole/chamber), with char giving the root type (tap root, fine roots, complex mass) as its subclasses.

label: Safety Chain Bar
existing_comment:
To describe DCJ:

DCJ This is used to record the location and condition of safety chains/bars on the  outgoing connections. Characterisation The following information:  safety chain present with no defects (A); safety chain missing (with evidence that one was provided) (B); safety chain defective (C); safety chain in position but coated with debris (D); safety bar present with no defects (E); safety bar missing (with evidence that one was provided) (F); safety bar defective (G); safety bar in position but coated with debris (H)

label: Seam Covering Separation
din_clause: Table 4, BAK char1 (H); Table 10, DAK char1 (H)
comment: The material covering a seam in the lining has separated. Used for BAK char1 (H) and DAK char1 (H).

label: Settled Deposit
comment: Material has settled and deposited in the invert of the pipe, or in the invert/benching of a chamber. Used for BBC (pipe) and DBC (manhole/chamber), with char giving the deposit type (fine, coarse, hard/compacted) as its subclasses.

label: Sewer Curvature
comment: The route of the drain or sewer deviates by a prefabricated bend rather than at a joint (a curved pipeline), explicitly excluding angular joint displacement (BAJ C). Used for BCC, with char1 (Left/Right) and char2 (Up/Down) recording horizontal and vertical curvature direction; DIN defines no equivalent code for manholes/chambers.

label: Silt
din_clause: Table 7, BDG char (B); Table 13, DDG char (B)
comment: The view is obstructed by suspended silt in the water. Used for BDG char (B) and DDG char (B).

label: Silt Pit
existing_comment:
Used to describe DCN.

Characterisation The following information:  pit not defective (A); pit defective (B).

label: Soil Visible Through Defect
comment: Soil from outside the pipe or chamber wall is visible through an existing defect. Used for BAO (pipe) and DAO (manhole/chamber).

label: Spalling
din_clause: Table 4, BAF char1 (B); Table 10, DAF char1 (B)
comment: Small fragments breaking away from the surface of the pipe or chamber fabric, one of the surface-damage types. Used for BAF char1 (B) and DAF char1 (B).

label: Special Node Type
comment: A node type defined locally by the employing authority, coded with an X-prefixed value rather than one of the standard's own letters. Used for BCD (X) and BCE (X).

label: Steam
din_clause: Table 7, BDG char (C); Table 13, DDG char (C)
comment: The view is obstructed by steam or condensation. Used for BDG char (C) and DDG char (C).

label: Structural Defect
comment: Groups the standard's fabric-condition codes (BA.. for pipes, DA.. for nodes); deformation, fissures, breaks, defective brickwork, surface damage, linings, repairs and similar; describing damage to the physical structure of the pipe or chamber. SDCO uses StructuralDefect as the parent of these classes, referenced via hasPipeFabricDamage/hasNodeFabricDamage.

label: Surface
comment: The surface of the pipe or chamber has been damaged by mechanical action or chemical attack (including metal corrosion). Used for BAF (pipe) and DAF (manhole/chamber), with subclasses for each char1 damage type and the Cause subtree giving char2.

label: Surface Crack Fissure
din_clause: Table 4, BAB char1 (A); Table 10, DAB char1 (A)
comment: The mildest fissure type: a crack confined to the surface, not extending through the wall. Used for BAB char1 (A) and DAB char1 (A).

label: Sweating Infiltration
din_clause: Table 5, BBF char (A); Table 11, DBF char1 (A)
comment: The mildest infiltration extent: a slow ingress of water with no visible drips. Used for BBF char (A) and DBF char1 (A).

label: Turbid Wastewater
din_clause: Table 7, BDD (C); BDE char1 (C); DDE char1 (C)
comment: The wastewater is turbid (cloudy) but not additionally coloured. Used for BDD (C), BDE char1 (C) and DDE char1 (C); SDCO also maps the combined 'turbid and coloured' value (E) onto this class alongside ColouredWastewater.

label: U Shape Connecting Pipeline
comment: A pipe cross-section with a circular invert and a flat top, joined by parallel sides. Used for DCG char1 (D).

label: Unable To Lift Cover
comment: A node-inspection-only termination reason: the manhole or inspection chamber cover could not be removed. Used only for DDC char1 (A); pipe inspections have no equivalent BDC value since they involve no cover to lift.

label: Unknown Wastewater
comment: Records that the incoming pipe's wastewater could not be observed because the water level in the main pipe was too high, using the standard's YY 'not observable' code. Used only for BDE char1 (YY); DIN gives no equivalent YY provision for DDE.

label: Ventilation Pipe Connection
comment: The connection is a ventilation pipe rather than a wastewater-carrying connection. Used for DCA char1 (F).

label: Venturi Flow Control
comment: A measuring flume (e.g. a venturi) used to gauge flow rather than to physically control it. Used for DCK char1 (G).

label: Vermin
comment: Vermin (rats, cockroaches or other animals) actually observed in or around the pipe or chamber. Used for BBH (pipe) and DBH (manhole/chamber), with char1 giving the animal type and char2 the location.

label: Void Visible Through Defect
comment: A void in the ground outside the pipe or chamber wall is visible through an existing defect. Used for BAP (pipe) and DAP (manhole/chamber).

label: Vortex Flow Control
comment: A vortex-type flow control device, which limits flow rate using a swirling flow pattern rather than a moving mechanical part. Used for DCK char1 (D).

label: Wall Infiltration
existing_comment: Infiltration through the wall of the manhole or inspection chamber

label: Wall Part Repair
comment: Part of the manhole or inspection chamber wall was replaced during the repair. Used for DCB char (A); the pipe-side code (BCB char1 A, 'pipe replaced') is instead mapped to the separate PipeReplacedRepair class, which has no someValuesFrom wiring to hasPipeInventoryFeature, so BCB (A) individuals are not currently materialized into a specific repair-type class.

label: Wastewater
din_clause: Table 7, BDD/BDE char1; Table 13, DDE char1
comment: The visual appearance of the wastewater in the pipe or chamber (clear, discontinued code, turbid, coloured, or turbid-and-coloured), shared by the water-level and incoming-flow codes. Used for BDD, BDE char1 and DDE char1, with the specific appearance values as its subclasses.

label: Water Level
comment: The level of wastewater above the invert of the pipe or chamber. Used for BDD (pipe, char gives the wastewater's appearance from the Wastewater subtree) and DDD (manhole/chamber, recorded only via the vertical location, with no characterization).

label: Weld Failure
comment: A failure in a weld in the fabric of the pipe or chamber. Used for BAM (pipe, char: longitudinal/circumferential/helical) and DAM (manhole/chamber, char: vertical/horizontal/inclined).

label: Widens Channel
comment: The channel widens in the direction of flow. Used for DCI char2 (B).

label: Working Benching
comment: Records that the benching was inspected and found not defective. Used for DCH char (B).

label: Working Channel
comment: Records that the channel was inspected and found not defective. Used for DCI char1 (B).

label: Wrongly Connected Incoming Surface Water Pipe
din_clause: Table 7, BDE char2 (B); Table 13, DDE char2 (A)
comment: Surface water is observed discharging into a wastewater drain or sewer, indicating a wrongly connected surface-water pipe. Used for BDE char2 (B) and DDE char2 (A); the two codes swap the A/B ordering of this and the wastewater case.

label: Wrongly Connected Incoming Wastewater Pipe
din_clause: Table 7, BDE char2 (A); Table 13, DDE char2 (B)
comment: Wastewater is observed discharging into a surface-water drain or sewer, indicating a wrongly connected foul pipe. Used for BDE char2 (A) and DDE char2 (B); the two codes swap the A/B ordering of this and the surface-water case.
